retire.reason: Duplicate in disguise. The structures pass and t1 recorded the same strokes under different kinds. The block's evidence (a vertical edge at u ~1333, v 850-880, and a top line near v 848) and the box's outline (u 1332-1360, v 845-900) are one shape. At zoom 8 that shape is the front-west corner of a squared block, not a box with a gabled lid. (1) Its front's west edge is vertical at u 1333-1334 from v 858 down to the foot, which is measured at v 901-904 over u 1335-1345. (2) Its front top edge is level at v 859 from u 1334 to ~1358, where the tied sack hides it. (3) What t1 read as the lid's peak is the top's west edge receding up-right, (1334, 857) -> (1351, 843), slope about -0.82. No falling second slope follows east of 1352: only the pointing man's sleeve at v ~836 and the sack's tied neck at (1355-1362, 868-875) are there. The front face is 43 px tall (v 859-902); the west block's is 47 (v 852-899), and the west block's top edge recedes at -0.80. The corner stands straight below the passage's east jamb, whose strokes run at u 1333-1349 from the lintel down to v ~760 (z_passage.jpg). Likewise the west block's passage end lies below the west jamb (u 1199-1209). Both front corners sit 14-16 px outside their jambs' line, so the gate is symmetrical. Its fill is a mottled darker wash, not the west block's diagonal hatching; that face is a side face, and this is a front. Keep the block, with the box as its other reading (below). Remove the box from S7.grp.gatehouse_1240 and reword the texts that name 'a dark box'.

lessons: **Check for duplicates across kinds, not only within one kind.** The merge flags things of the same kind under 30 px apart. On S7, one unit read 20 px of strokes as a structure (a second gate block) and the other as a prop (a box with a peaked lid). Both survived the merge. List every pair of entities of different kinds whose points lie under 30 px apart, and look at each pair that isn't an obvious neighbour on one zoom-6 crop.

**A small box's 'peak' or 'lid' may be its top's receding edge.** In this oblique view a box's top shows as a parallelogram whose side edge rises up-right at about the receding slope (-0.8 on S7). Before you record a gabled lid, look for the second, falling slope.

**To settle a faint extra figure, look for a closed head** (hair wash, face, chin line) at zoom 6 in greyscale. Long parallel strokes running unbroken from waist to hem are robe folds: S7's 'second child' at the doctor's was folds.

**Measure short receding edges from the pixels.** Trace the lower boundary of the stroke per column (3x3 mean below a threshold) and fit a line. On S7's gate block, two eye readings of one 30-px edge gave -0.80 and -1.08; the trace gave -0.87 over the whole foot and -1.10 over its straight front part, where the line bends at the jamb.
